how: An initial placer supplies coordinates and receives a direct reply reporting added blue pixels
Calls recruit people to build and enlarge the national flag
A participant directly answers the starter with a bare report of adding blue pixels
Flag enlargement and lettering proposals coexist with an avocado proposal, so the broad design element fits more accurately than an exclusively national-flag placement
Members report their placements and the repair of the final pixel
The initial coordinate instantiates locating the work without establishing a complete agreed template
Members offer bots as an alternative to manual placement, urge unattended operation, and report running them
The reported democratic redesign choice places this room within the claim's decided-order minority without testing the cross-room prevalence claim
Participants retrospectively describe doubts about having enough capacity to fight and redesign simultaneously
Guard calls, concentration on fewer flags, automated cleaning and final-pixel repairs make preservation an explicit shared task
A visitor denies responsibility for invading while another speaker separates streamer intent from the conduct of his community
Coexistence appeals, rejection of retaliation and rebuilding the rainbow show restraint alongside flag defence
Neighbours are invited to negotiate compromise while other builders are told the banner is already claimed
Offered help and reciprocal thanks instantiate cooperation, while the Armenian greeting alone establishes only the element's greeting range
A coalition roll-call and thanks to alliance brokers support participation in alliances without exposing their internal bargains
Alliance brokers are credited retrospectively but no particular envoy's proposal-carrying itinerary is observed
A flag-heart builder thanks hosts for allowing hearts and distinguishes the accepted contribution from an independently made duplicate
Disowning duplicate construction and distrusting an agreement under continuing damage do not establish a dispute over who can bind other placers
Deleting rainbow road is proposed and one member reports a white pixel on the USSR flag without establishing a collective raid
Visitors and participants contest invasion, threats and relevance, while a rival visitor offers congratulations in a personal capacity
Capacity doubts are followed in the retrospective account by redesign and continued repair rather than a documented relocation
Victory announcements credit allies, brokers and bot administrators while individual participants report unequal contributions
Members reconstruct the last-minute redesign and direct readers to the invasion and defence in a timelapse
An invitation to celebrate on Discord does not establish a successor project or a decision to preserve a permanent collective
The absurd dog-shoe joke supports limited April Fools play without establishing a takeover or a hoax behind the canvas call
A complaint about the canvas flood is followed by an explicit instruction to keep the front page clean through a megathread
Occupation and independence-war jokes, national pride and claims about fitting e-Estonia make the canvas effort an occasion for national identification
Naming Team Soviet and later joking about occupation do not establish that a pre-canvas quarrel was carried into the event
Retrospective occupation jokes and an unexplained USSR pixel cannot establish historical rivalry as an explicitly stated motive in an earlier attack turn
Replies correct a rival visitor's account of a vote from allowing the head to stay into choosing whether to redesign while fighting
A speaker explicitly makes distrust of a possible agreement depend on continuing bot damage to the flag
Repair automation is supported but timer-pressure causation remains untested because the coded recruitment offer instead invokes avoiding manual placement
Celebration and a later timelapse reference are observed without an explicit dependence making celebration the cause of recording
An organizer explicitly credits allies with helping fend off attacks, although the intervening shortage of hands is not independently established
A compromise invitation and later thanks for cooperation do not identify a particular border deal as the cause of traded help
The visible duplicate-heart clarification and damaged negotiation do not supply both a binding agreement and a subsequent dispute over representative authority
Capacity doubts need not culminate in relocation when participants choose simultaneous redesign and continued defence of the existing work
The perceived flood of canvas material is answered by a megathread instruction, without establishing moderator enforcement or attributing the flood to every call
The timelapse and invitation to celebrate do not show recording generating a successor project
Builders route planning into chat explicitly to avoid accidentally working against one another
An organizer explains artistic redesign as intended to ease alliance recruitment, without demonstrating that the expected recruitment effect occurred
An organizer reports that opponents not understanding the language gave redesign discussion an advantage
Distinguish running a shared bot from following its master source because one contributor disclaims using that bot despite discussing its source
A possible agreement remains contingent on ending ongoing damage that participants explicitly say destroys their trust
Negotiation encounters a stated refusal to accept threats as currency rather than treating coercion as an ordinary bargaining term
After-fight contest includes mock medicine and literal cooking play, which cannot all be explained as national-history analogies
Participants undertake redesign during active defence rather than requiring preservation of the existing image to finish before design work resumes
A locating coordinate and a retrospective democratic-design account do not establish design debate being settled by publication of an agreed template
Compromise invitations and calls to rebuild the rainbow do not identify a settled border as the reason for restraint
Thanks for alliances and defence establish cooperation but leave the timing and motive of coalition formation inside unseen coordination
Contest talk can arise from being the target of an incoming attack rather than from the host room's own attack call
Recruitment and reported placing coexist but the surviving coded passages do not identify a particular call as causing the later contribution
An initial placement precedes further calls without an explicit passage identifying the starter as the reason for those calls
A guard call directly answers the announcement that the flag is flying
The shared flag being completed supplies the stated object of praise and thanks
A direct bare contribution report answers the starter's proposal without demonstrating that every reader owes or supplies an answer
Recruitment and a later attack proposal are visible without a supported link making recruitment turn participants toward attacking
An upkeep-based refusal of retaliation survives but its specific attack-call prompt is not coded sufficiently to establish the proposed exchange mechanism
The rainbow-road attack proposal and a separate compromise invitation do not form an observed attack-to-negotiation sequence
